verses.text: At that time Yahweh said to me, “Cut two stone tablets like the first, and come up to me onto the mountain, and make an ark of wood.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets which you broke, and you shall put them in the ark.”
So I made an ark of acacia wood, and cut two stone tablets like the first, and went up onto the mountain, having the two tablets in my hand.

He wrote on the tablets, according to the first writing, the ten commandments, which Yahweh spoke to you on the mountain out of the middle of the fire in the day of the assembly: and Yahweh gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the mountain, and put the tablets in the ark which I had made; and there they are as Yahweh commanded me.
(The children of Israel traveled from Beeroth Bene Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died, and there he was buried; and Eleazar his son ministered in the priest’s office in his place.
From there they traveled to Gudgodah; and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of brooks of water.
At that time Yahweh set apart the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of Yahweh’s covenant, to stand before Yahweh to minister to him, and to bless in his name, to this day.
Therefore Levi has no portion nor inheritance with his brothers; Yahweh is his inheritance, according as Yahweh your God spoke to him.)
I stayed on the mountain, as at the first time, forty days and forty nights: and Yahweh listened to me that time also; Yahweh would not destroy you.
Yahweh said to me, “Arise, take your journey before the people; and they shall go in and possess the land, which I swore to their fathers to give to them.”
Now, Israel, what does Yahweh your God require of you, but to fear Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
to keep Yahweh’s commandments and statutes, which I command you today for your good?
Behold, to Yahweh your God belongs heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth, with all that is therein.
Only Yahweh had a delight in your fathers to love them, and he chose their offspring  after them, even you above all peoples, as it is today.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiff-necked.
For Yahweh your God, he is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great God, the mighty, and the awesome, who doesn’t respect persons, nor takes reward.
He does execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loves the foreigner, in giving him food and clothing.
Therefore love the foreigner; for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You shall fear Yahweh your God; you shall serve him; and you shall cling to him, and you shall swear by his name.
He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things, which your eyes have seen.
Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy persons; and now Yahweh your God has made you as the stars of the sky for multitude.

footnotes.content: Mercy wears practical shoes. After Moses broke the first tablets in anger, the Lord didn't say 'You've ruined everything'—He said 'Cut two more.' There's something tender in that: the Lord works with what we've broken and asks us to help repair it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God would rewrite the same ten commandments, word for word. No grudge, no changes to punish our failings. The Lord's word is so firm that even our rebellion cannot alter it—only our obedience or disobedience to it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Acacia wood—hard, durable, native to Sinai—became the material of second chances. Moses cut and carried with his own hands. We're invited, always, to be part of restoration, not mere spectators of God's grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Ten Commandments inscribed twice—first in fire, now by God's own hand. The law isn't arbitrary or distant; it flows from the character of the one who speaks from flame and yet writes with care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses placed them in the ark 'as Yahweh commanded me.' Simple obedience—no hesitation, no negotiation. This is how the covenant is carried: in a wooden box, protected and honored, from camp to camp across the wilderness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Beeroth Bene Jaakan, Moserah—dusty names that frame a somber fact: Aaron, the first high priest, died in the wilderness and was buried there. The priesthood passed to Eleazar without ceremony or fanfare, just faithful continuation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Gudgodah, Jotbathah—'a land of brooks of water.' The Lord remembered to guide Israel not just with fire and cloud but with the small mercy of water where thirst threatened. Every detail of the journey was held in His care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The tribe of Levi was set apart—not to own land but to bear God's covenant and stand before Him. This is a strange honor: to own nothing but to hold everything that matters. Jesus would later teach us that losing everything for His kingdom is the truest gain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Yahweh is his inheritance.' The Levites received no vineyard, no pasture, no corner of Canaan—only God. And what a wealth that was. We too are called to find our riches not in what we hold but in knowing Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Forty days and forty nights—the same solemn period as before. Moses fasted, interceded, stood in the gap between a holy God and a stiff-necked people. And the Lord listened. His patience is not weakness; it is the deep mercy of a God who hears even when we stumble.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Arise, take your journey'—not 'Now you can rest,' but 'Press on.' The covenant was renewed not for comfort but to send Israel forward into the promise. God's grace isn't a stopping place; it's a road.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'What does Yahweh your God require of you?' Everything, really—but Moses asks it gently. Fear, obedience, love, service with the whole heart: not a burden but a summary of what it means to be alive before God. This is the law's true heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'For your good'—the commandments aren't God's whim but His gift. They protect us, shape us, show us the way of blessing. When we keep them, we're not earning favor; we're accepting the invitation to flourish.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Heaven of heavens, earth, all that is therein—everything belongs to Yahweh. We hold nothing absolutely, own nothing finally. This truth, when it settles in, brings peace: we can let go because He never lets go.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God 'had a delight in your fathers.' Not because they were worthy but because He loved them. And then He chose their children—us—'above all peoples.' This preference, this particularism, is the scandal of grace: that God should set His affection on one people, and through them bless all nations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Circumcise the foreskin of your heart.' Not just the body but the will, the affection, the stubbornness. God asks for an inward turning, a softening. To follow Him is to be remade from within, and it begins when we stop resisting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God of gods, Lord of lords—awesome above all powers. And yet 'doesn't respect persons, nor takes reward.' The mighty God shows no favoritism, takes no bribes. In His sight, the widow and the wanderer stand as surely as kings. This is the foundation of justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: God executes justice for the fatherless and widow, and loves the foreigner by meeting their hunger and cold. The Lord's love isn't sentimental; it's active, particular, embodied in bread and clothing. We meet Him when we feed the hungry.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'You were foreigners in the land of Egypt'—the appeal is to memory and gratitude. Because Israel knew the stranger's grief, they are bound to love the stranger. Mercy, once received, becomes a debt paid forward, not a luxury.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fear, serve, cling, swear—all verbs of bond and union. To fear the Lord is not trembling before a tyrant but holding fast to the one who alone is worthy. 'Cling to Him' as a child clings to a parent, or as the vine clings to the trellis.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'He is your praise'—your song, your reason for joy. The Lord isn't a stern accountant tallying your debts; He is the subject of your worship, the one who has done great and awesome things before your very eyes. Gratitude is the response that turns us toward Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seventy persons became as many as the stars—a promise kept, a multiplication that only God can account. The arc of Israel's story is a testimony: the Lord makes the impossible multiply. What seems small in His hands becomes beyond counting.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
